title: AIP-C01 Skill 1.4.5: Keep the Vector Store Fresh
html:
AIP-C01 Skill 1.4.5: Keep the Vector Store Fresh

A hands-on lab with incremental sync, drift detection, S3 events, Lambda and EventBridge Scheduler. Task 1.4, post 5 of 6.

[IMAGE: cover-1-4-5.png — alt: "Skill 1.4.5: Keeping the vector store fresh"]

AIP-C01 Hands-on Labs · Domain 1 · Task 1.4: Design and implement vector store solutions · Post 5 of 6. Hands-on lab, about 30 minutes.

In April the returns window for hedge trimmers changes from 14 days to 21. The policy document in S3 is updated the same morning. The assistant keeps saying 14 days for another week, because nobody synced the knowledge base. A vector store is a copy of your documents, and copies go stale. This skill is about keeping that copy current automatically, including deletions.

What AWS says

Skill 1.4.5: Design and deploy data maintenance systems to ensure that vector stores contain current and accurate information for FM augmentation (for example, by using incremental update mechanisms, real-time change detection systems, automated synchronization workflows, scheduled refresh pipelines).

What it means in plain words

  • Incremental updates: re-embed only what changed, and remove what was deleted, instead of rebuilding everything.
  • Real-time change detection: notice a change when it happens (an S3 event, a webhook) or find drift by comparing the source with the index.
  • Automated synchronization: a change triggers a sync with no person involved.
  • Scheduled refresh: a regular sync as a safety net, and the normal method for connector sources.

[IMAGE: t1-4-5-freshness.png — alt: "Keeping the vector store fresh: incremental sync, event-driven sync, scheduled sync, direct ingestion and drift check, with delay and use"]

What we're going to do

  1. Ask the knowledge base from the Skill 1.4.2 lab about hedge trimmers: 14 days.
  2. Update the 2026 policy to the April version and delete the 2025 policy from S3.
  3. Detect, before syncing, which documents are stale and which are orphaned in the index.
  4. Run an incremental sync and read its statistics; ask again: 21 days.
  5. Automate it: a Lambda function triggered by S3 events, plus a nightly EventBridge Scheduler schedule.

What you'll learn

  • What a knowledge base sync actually does with changed and deleted files.
  • How to detect drift between a source and the index.
  • How to combine an event-driven fast path with a scheduled backstop.
  • What to do when changes must appear in seconds.

What you'll need

  • Time and cost: about 30 minutes, a few cents
  • Region: us-west-2
  • Access: Python 3.10+ with boto3; LAB_BUCKET, KB_ID and DS_ID from the Skill 1.4.2 lab; permission to create a Lambda function and an EventBridge schedule
  • Files: github.com/prasanth2006z/aip-c01-labs, folder domain-1/task-1.4/skill-1.4.5-freshness

The lab

Part 1: Incremental sync by hand

Step 1: Ask before the change

export LAB_BUCKET=your-bucket-name KB_ID=XXXXXXXXXX DS_ID=XXXXXXXXXX
python freshness.py ask

The top result is the 2026 policy: hedge trimmers, 14 days.

Step 2: Change the source

python freshness.py change

The script uploads the April version of returns-policy-2026.txt (21 days, keeping its author and published metadata) and deletes returns-policy-2025.txt with its metadata file. Ask again now and you still get 14 days: S3 has changed, the index hasn't.

Step 3: Detect drift

python freshness.py detect

The script lists every object under kb-docs/ and every document the data source has indexed (ListKnowledgeBaseDocuments), then compares them:

STALE     kb-docs/returns-policy-2026.txt  (changed 10:42:07, indexed 09:15:31)
current   kb-docs/shipping-times.txt
current   kb-docs/store-returns-uk.txt
current   kb-docs/warranty-power-tools.txt
ORPHANED  kb-docs/returns-policy-2025.txt  (deleted from S3, still in the index)

An orphan is the dangerous one: a document that no longer exists but can still be quoted. Run the same comparison on a schedule and publish the counts as CloudWatch metrics, and you have an alarm for a knowledge base that has fallen behind.

Step 4: Incremental sync

python freshness.py sync

Look at the statistics:

numberOfDocumentsScanned            ...
numberOfModifiedDocumentsIndexed    1
numberOfDocumentsDeleted            1
numberOfNewDocumentsIndexed         0

The sync scans every file but re-embeds only the one that changed and removes the one that was deleted. You pay for embedding one document, not five. That's what “incremental” means here, and it's built in: every StartIngestionJob on an S3 data source works this way.

Step 5: Ask again

python freshness.py ask

21 days, from the April policy. The 2025 policy no longer appears at all.

Part 2: Automate it

sync_on_change.py is a Lambda handler that starts a sync. It's triggered two ways:

  1. Create the function: Python runtime, name kb-sync, handler sync_on_change.handler, environment variables KB_ID and DS_ID. Give its role bedrock:StartIngestionJob on the knowledge base.
  2. Fast path, S3 events: bucket → Properties → Event notifications → all object create and all object removal events, prefix kb-docs/, destination kb-sync.
  3. Safety net, a schedule: EventBridge Scheduler → cron 0 2 * * ? * (02:00 every day) → target kb-sync.
  4. Test: upload any .txt file under kb-docs/, then check the function's logs and the data source's sync history.
try:
    agent.start_ingestion_job(knowledgeBaseId=KB_ID, dataSourceId=DS_ID,
                              description=f"triggered by {source}")
except agent.exceptions.ConflictException:
    # A sync is already running; the nightly schedule catches anything it misses.
    print({"skipped": "sync already running"})

Why both? Only one sync can run per data source at a time. If ten files arrive in a minute, the first event starts a sync and some of the others are skipped. That sync may already have scanned past those files, so the scheduled run is what guarantees they're picked up. Events give speed; the schedule gives a guarantee.

When minutes are too slow

A sync takes minutes. If a change must be searchable within seconds (a product recall, a pricing error), push that one document with direct ingestion, as in the Skill 1.4.4 lab, or delete it by ID. Keep the sync as the normal path.

Changing the embedding model

Vectors from different embedding models can't be compared. If you switch models, re-embed everything into a new index or knowledge base, test it, then switch the application over. Never mix models in one index.

Common pitfalls

  • ConflictException: a sync is already running on that data source. Retry later or rely on the schedule.
  • Deleted documents still quoted: deletions reach the index only when a sync runs (or when you delete by ID). Make sure removal events trigger a sync too.
  • Lambda triggered by its own writes: if your function writes metadata files under the same prefix, filter by suffix or use a separate prefix to avoid loops.
  • Lambda can't start the job: its role needs bedrock:StartIngestionJob on the knowledge base ARN.

Clean up

This is the last Task 1.4 lab, so remove everything the task created:

  1. EventBridge Scheduler: delete the schedule.
  2. S3: delete the event notification, then the kb-docs/ objects.
  3. Lambda: delete kb-sync, its log group and its role.
  4. Bedrock: delete the aip-lab-kb knowledge base (this deletes its data sources).
  5. S3 Vectors: delete the vector index and vector bucket that quick create made (S3 console → Vector buckets).
  6. IAM: delete the knowledge base service role (AmazonBedrockExecutionRoleForKnowledgeBase_...).

What to remember

  • StartIngestionJob is incremental: it re-embeds changed documents and removes deleted ones.
  • S3 event → Lambda → sync for near real time; EventBridge Scheduler → sync as the backstop.
  • One sync per data source at a time; handle ConflictException.
  • Seconds, not minutes → direct ingestion or delete by document ID.
  • Detect drift by comparing source objects with indexed documents; alarm on it.
  • New embedding model → re-embed everything into a new index, then switch.

The exam scenarios for this skill are in post 6 of this task: Task 1.4 Exam Notes.

References

  • Sync your data with your knowledge base
  • Amazon S3 event notifications
